summary: Three good-length passages (909, 956 and 991 words) with difficulty rising properly, from a clear history of locks to a C1-level argumentative psychology text. The keys were sound; I removed one ambiguous gap (Q5), put the Yes/No/Not Given questions back into passage order and tightened one sentence ending. The main weakness is that Passage 2 tests several facts twice across its three question sets.
strengths: Passage 3 is genuinely C1: argumentative and hedged, with the writer's view to be inferred (Q29, Q34).
T/F/NG and Y/N/NG are clean: FALSE/NO items are contradicted, NOT GIVEN items are genuinely unaddressed.
A good mix of IELTS types: sentence completion, TFNG, matching information, summary completion, matching people, MCQ, YNNG, sentence endings.
MCQ distractors are plausible and each is tied to something in the text.

issues.problem: Two defensible answers: 'the authorities offered a locksmith his freedom' also fits, since the convict was 'a locksmith by trade'.
issues.change: Prompt now reads 'offered a ______ with locksmithing skills his freedom and a sum of money', so only 'convict' fits; explain updated.

issues.problem: Y/N/NG not in passage order: Q33 (older people, paragraph 7) came before Q34 (paragraph 6) and Q35 (paragraph 5).
issues.change: Swapped the content of Q33 and Q35: Q33 is now 'difficult aims' (NO), Q35 'Older people' (NOT GIVEN). Pattern Y N N Y NG. Any results saved before this change hold Q33/Q35 in the old order.

issues.problem: Ending G 'can give a misleading impression of what the emotion actually does' could also be argued for Q40 (confusion with collective nostalgia gives nostalgia its bad reputation).
issues.change: Ending G reworded to 'says more about a person's situation than about what the emotion does', which fits Q39 only; explain and pair updated.

issues.problem: Weak or broken paraphrase pairs: one side contained in the other (e.g. 'journeys' / 'urban journeys'), or the two sides meaning different things (e.g. 'wait longest' / 'the order in which facilities are provided').
issues.change: Replaced with real paraphrases, e.g. 'the order in which cycle lanes get built' / 'the order in which facilities are provided', 'merchants' / 'Traders', 'bring to mind an event from their own past' / 'recalling a nostalgic event', 'has come through something' / 'have survived hardship'.
Added ['the double-acting lever tumbler', "Barron's lever lock"], the paraphrase that locates this NOT GIVEN item.

issues.problem: Passage 2 tests the same facts twice: Q14/Q20 (Ferreira, network), Q16/Q24 (shopkeepers' belief), Q17/Q21 (junctions), Q18/Q25 (Tanaka, building order), Q22/Q26 (Duarte, theft). A student who finds one gets the other almost free, which weakens discrimination.
issues.change: Suggest re-targeting one of each pair to unused details: the 1973 oil shock or Stop de Kindermoord (A), the 'interested but concerned' sixty per cent (B), Halvorsen's twenty-to-one health ratio (D), the Utrecht garage (E), one car space holding ten bicycles (F), e-bikes and cargo bikes missing from plans (G).

issues.problem: Q2 is pure scanning: the prompt copies the passage sentence almost word for word. Q1-6 are on the easy side overall, acceptable for Passage 1.
issues.change: Suggest paraphrasing the prompt, e.g. 'Some Roman keys became so tiny that they could be worn like a piece of ______.' Left without a pair (nothing to pair).

issues.problem: NOT GIVEN item has no genuine paraphrase to pair.
